---
title: "Consul: Registration and Discovery"
description: "A worked microservices lesson using the shop-services example."
---

**Course source:** Day 1 §5.1–§5.5. **Running system:** Order, Product, and User services.

## Keep the same service discovery need

The course introduces **Consul** as an alternative registry and covers its agent model, registering a shop service, discovering instances and using key/value data.

The architectural goal is unchanged: Order asks for a healthy Product endpoint by service identity, not by a hard-coded host.

## What changes compared with Eureka?

Consul combines service discovery with health-check information and a key/value interface. A service may be registered through an agent and discovered through HTTP or DNS interfaces. Health checks help consumers avoid endpoints known to be unhealthy.

~~~text
Product instance -> Consul agent -> Consul catalogue
Order ----------- service discovery query -----^
~~~

The **catalogue** and the **health view** are related but different: a registered service may not currently pass its checks. Consumers should use the discovery interface that supplies the intended health semantics.

## Key/value data is not a database replacement

The course uses Consul KV to illustrate centrally stored settings. It can hold small configuration values, but that does not make it a general-purpose transactional storage engine for orders or customer records.

~~~text
shop/product/currency = JPY
shop/order/max-items  = 10
~~~

These are conceptual keys, not a prescribed production namespace. Access control and change propagation must be designed separately.

## Choosing a discovery system

Evaluate who operates it, health semantics, failover behaviour, authentication, consistency needs and platform integration. Kubernetes DNS may cover simple discovery; Consul can be useful across heterogeneous runtimes and network boundaries.

**Historical source check:** The course's discussion of project availability and replacements is time-specific. Always consult current vendor release and support documentation before choosing a registry.

## Test your reasoning

Name the component that owns this responsibility, explain its behaviour during a failure, and identify one configuration or metric you would verify in production.
